Applications: create / edit / deactivate, link teams and review related budgets.

tma.title: What is this module for?
items: Handle application changes and incidents requiring analysis, budget or release.
BUILD team: application owner, developers, optional user lead gate.
On resolve: proposes one day (8 h) on the assignee timesheet.

support.title: What is this module for?
items: Helpdesk: user questions, access, light incidents without full TMA cycle.
DESK team: Support profile, threaded replies, no quote or analysis dossier.
On resolve: proposes one hour on the timesheet.

maintenance.title: What is this module for?
items: Operations and infra work without TMA overhead (fixes, deployments, ops).
RUN team: tracked in consumed days, no mandatory analysis artefacts.
On complete: proposes days × 8 h on the timesheet.

demandes.title: Configure request channels
items: ESN: enable TMA + User support for maintenance + helpdesk contracts.
Structured IT dept: add Operations & work for the RUN team.
Small team: TMA alone is often enough — disable other channels.

New SSO users receive the default profile configured below.

workflows.title: Design a validation workflow
items: A workflow defines steps (states) and allowed actions between them (transitions).
Each business module (leave, TMA…) relies on a predefined workflow code.
Exactly one initial state and at least one final state are required.
Transitions drive the action buttons shown in business screens.
Change with care: an incorrect workflow can block validations.

cra.title: What is this module for?
items: Enter and track monthly activity reports per mission.
Submit → manager validation workflow, with commercial info for client PDF.
Access planning and Gantt views to monitor workload and open timesheets.

conges.title: What is this module for?
items: Submit and track leave requests (paid leave, RTT, sick leave…).
View balances and history of approved absences.
Managers approve requests from the Validation tab.

budget.title: What is this module for?
items: Track work-unit budgets: planned vs consumed days per mission.
View consumption rate and overrun alerts.
Open a budget to detail lines and adjust forecasts.

invoicing.title: What is this module for?
items: View and create client invoices (module enabled under Organisation → Modules).
« From a timesheet » wizard: prefilled preview (client, hours, rate) then edit before create.
Send a proforma by email with a client validation link; on validation, convert to invoice and auto-send.
Also generate drafts from Deliverables → Create invoices, or via manual entry.
Rate: mission TJM, else application default TJM, else company default TJM (converted to €/h).

missions.title: What is this module for?
items: Reference missions and link them to a client.
Assign collaborators to each mission for timesheets and budgets.
Create a new mission from the button at top right.

prestations.title: What is this module for?
items: Validate service timesheets before invoicing or export.
Create invoice drafts for definitive timesheets (Invoicing write and CRA validate permissions).
Filter, sort and export the validated batch (XML).

dashboard.title: What is this module for?
items: Overview: KPIs for active modules, pending validations, alerts.
Quick access to modules via cards and shortcuts.
AI briefing summarises recent activity when the module is enabled.

states.en_attente: Starting state: the request was just submitted.
states.valide: Final state: the request was approved.
states.refuse: Final state: the request was rejected.
states.en_attente_creation: Starting state when chef utilisateur validation is required.
states.ouverte: Default starting state or after creation validation.
states.affectee: A responsible person was assigned to the incident.
states.resolue: Final state: the incident is resolved.
states.rework: The incident was reopened for correction.
states.preparee: Starting state: timesheet validated, invoice created as prepared.
states.proforma: Proforma sent to the client, awaiting decision.
states.facture_envoyee: Final state: the client approved the proforma (invoice email send remains best-effort).
states.proforma_refusee: The client rejected the proforma; re-emission is possible.

howto.title: How to design this workflow?
howto.step_states: Define steps: one initial state (start), intermediate states, and at least one final state.
howto.step_transitions: Connect states with actions (e.g. approve, reject, assign) — these become buttons in the app.
howto.step_roles: Optionally restrict an action to specific profiles; otherwise it is open to all.
howto.step_effects: Optional: configure emails when entering a state or when firing an action (custom recipients).
howto.step_save: Save then test from the related business module.
howto.leave_example: Leave example: Pending → approve → Approved, or reject → Rejected.
howto.tma_example: TMA example: Awaiting creation → validate_creation → Open → assign → Assigned → resolve → Resolved, with reopen → Rework.
howto.cra_proforma_example: Invoicing example: Prepared → emit_proforma → Proforma → validate_client → Invoice sent (or reject_client → reject then re-emit).

validation.one_initial: Exactly one state must be marked as initial.
validation.one_final: At least one state must be marked as final.
validation.orphan_transition: Each transition must link existing states.
validation.transition_action_required: Each transition must have an action.
validation.side_effect_invalid: A configured side effect is invalid.
validation.side_effect_subject_required: Each email must have a subject or body.
validation.too_many_side_effects: Too many side effects (maximum 10 per step).

effects.hint: Send an automatic email when this step is reached or when the action is fired.
effects.subject: Subject

howto.title: How it works
howto.item_code: The code identifies the rule (unique): use a stable slug (e.g. "leave-requested").
howto.item_trigger: The trigger is a business event name (e.g. "tma.demand.created").
howto.item_frequency: Frequency defines when notifications are sent (immediate or batched).
howto.item_template: Template is the message content that will be sent (text).

tooltip.trigger: Event name that triggers the send.

hint.code: Examples: "leave-requested", "tma-demand-created". Avoid spaces and uppercase letters.
hint.trigger: Example: "tma.demand.created". Must match a trigger supported by the API.
hint.frequency: Immediate sends right away. Other options batch and send at a fixed time.
hint.template: Write the message as it should appear in the notification.
hint.attach_pdf: Enables adding a PDF attachment when sending.
